info.title: Gödel Tally API
info.description: AI provider and model governance API

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: One-based page number. Out-of-range pages clamp to the last page.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 through 500; defaults to 100.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Inclusive observation time lower bound, Unix milliseconds.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Inclusive observation time upper bound, Unix milliseconds.

parameters.name: snapshot
parameters.description: Reuse the returned receipt-time cutoff while paging. Refresh to obtain a new cutoff.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive literal search across retained event metadata and event/source IDs.

parameters.name: outcome
parameters.description: Case-insensitive literal match against source action, result, or response code.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: newest (default) or oldest, with observation ID as a deterministic tie breaker.

additional_source_ips.description:
Other source addresses reported for the same device, such as a LAN address alongside the
public egress address. Connectors retain only validated IP literals and findings de-duplicate
them before persistence.

hostname.description:
Endpoint hostname when the source supplies one. Unlike `device_key`, this is retained so
operators can locate a device that is using an AI provider or model.

oneOf.description:
Bounded client/framework hint and explicit source agent ID. A client hint is not proof
that a particular agent process exists. Raw headers and user-agent strings are discarded.

AgentObservation.description:
Allowlisted agent metadata. Command lines are inspected transiently; only a recognized
executable/package signature is retained, never arbitrary arguments or source content.

account_key.description: Installation-local pseudonym for a provider account, subscription, or project account.

region.description: Provider-controlled region token. Connectors reject arbitrary or user-controlled values.

resource_key.description: Installation-local pseudonym derived from the provider-native resource identifier.

scope_key.description: Installation-local pseudonym for the containing subscription, project, or account scope.

ConnectorDeleteResponse.description:
Receipt for a removed connector: its schedule, sealed credentials, run receipts, and
ingestion ledger rows are gone. Observations it contributed are evidence and remain.

evidence_retained.description:
Always true: deleting a connector never deletes the evidence it already contributed.
The purge path is the only route that deletes observations.

friendly_name.description: The operator's own label for the removed instance, or null when they never named it.

content_retained.description: Always false: connectors keep metadata and digests, never source content.

credentials_sealed.description: True once the operator's credentials are stored sealed under `TALLY_SECRET_KEY`.

plaintext_secret_stored.description: Always false: Tally has no path that writes a credential to `PostgreSQL` in the clear.

friendly_name.description:
The operator's own label for this instance -- "Production EKS", "Staging cluster" --
which is what tells two connectors of the same type apart everywhere they are rendered.
Omit the field to keep whatever name is already stored; send an empty string to clear it.

ConnectorScheduleSourceInput.description:
A connector source as the operator filled it in on the console form.

Every field here is a value the operator typed, not the name of an environment variable:
account identifiers, endpoints, and API tokens alike. The values that are secret or
free-form never reach `config_refs` — [`connector_schedule_source`] routes them into the
sealed credential bundle stored on the job row.

display_name.description: Catalog label for the connector type; identical across every instance of that type.

friendly_name.description: The operator's own label for this instance, or null when they never named it.

sample.description: Illustrative sample connector; it has no credentials or polling schedule.

ConnectorSyncResponse.description:
Receipt for one on-demand run request. The run itself happens in the collector, which
claims the schedule on its next poll; this says the schedule is now due.

content_retained.description: Always false: an on-demand run reads the same bounded window as a scheduled one.

ConnectorSyncSweepResponse.description: Receipt for an on-demand run request across every registered schedule.

skipped_leased.description: Attempts already in flight, left on their existing lease.

skipped_paused.description: Paused schedules; an on-demand request does not resume them.

path_prefix.description: A registry-approved static prefix only; never a full path, query, or fragment.

EventFindingContext.description: Registry context for one exact event link; never includes aggregate user or endpoint data.

application_key.description: Installation-local pseudonym for the application, when the activity is app-scoped.

directory_key.description: Installation-local pseudonym for the source directory, when known.

display_label.description: Reserved for explicit operator metadata. Source-provided names are not copied here.

email.description:
Endpoint user email when the connector supplies one. This is retained for findings so an
operator can contact the user responsible for the observed usage.

source_subject.description:
Bounded source-native identity when the source does not report an email address. This may
be a login name or an immutable provider user ID and is retained so an operator can resolve
the responsible user in the source system.

casb_account_id.description:
Raw CASB account identifier is accepted only for in-memory installation-HMAC
pseudonymization and is never returned or stored.

oneOf.description:
Raw scope identifiers are accepted only for managed-cloud normalization, pseudonymized in
memory, and never returned or stored.

observed_at.description: Required for managed-cloud fixtures so preview and commit normalize to the same source time.

destination_endpoint_key.description: Installation-local pseudonym for the destination address within its provider network.

mapped_resource_key.description: Mapping-only: installation-local pseudonym matching managed-cloud inventory resource keys.

network_key.description: Installation-local pseudonym for the provider network/VPC/VNet.

source_endpoint_key.description: Installation-local pseudonym for the source address within its provider network.

valid_until.description: End of a source-authoritative flow or mapping validity window.

RequestClientKind.description: Allowlisted public client/framework names, never arbitrary user-agent text.

application_key.description: Installation-local pseudonym for the source integration/application instance.

oneOf.description: Bounded source-native capability state. This proves configuration, never user activity.
Source-native sanction metadata. Tally does not author or enforce this state.

tenant_key.description: Installation-local pseudonym for the source CASB account or tenant boundary.

ai_request.description:
True only when a connector recognized a bounded AI inference request signature while
normalizing transient HTTP metadata or content. Raw paths, bodies, headers, prompts, and
responses are never retained to prove this bit.

ai_request_evaluated.description:
True when HTTP path or body material was available and a connector completed the bounded
AI request signature check. A checked regular request must not be admitted solely because
its hostname belongs to a known provider.

scanner_fingerprint_id.description: Registry-controlled identifier for a matched, benign scanner fingerprint.

findings.description: Current registry context linked to the exact events on this page.

account_id.description:
Deprecated wire compatibility field. If present, the value must already be an
installation-local pseudonym; connectors must never place a raw provider account ID here.

namespace.description:
Deprecated wire compatibility field. If present, the value must already be an
installation-local pseudonym.

namespace_name.description:
Validated Kubernetes namespace name retained so operators can locate and remediate the
workload. This is never populated from labels, annotations, or workload content.

network_id.description:
Deprecated wire compatibility field. If present, the value must already be an
installation-local pseudonym.

runtime_image.description:
Exact bounded container image reference for the single allowlisted AI runtime matched in
this workload. Unrelated sidecar images are discarded.

runtime_registry_entry_id.description:
Registry-controlled public runtime identifier matched in memory from resource metadata.
Labels and annotations are never copied here.

workload_id.description:
Deprecated wire compatibility field. If present, the value must already be an
installation-local pseudonym.

workload_name.description:
Validated Kubernetes object name retained so operators can locate and remediate the
workload discovered by a read-only Kubernetes connector.
